components.content:
# IEC Electric Motor Duty Cycles

The International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) defines eight duty cycle designations (S1-S8) to describe electrical motor operating conditions:

## Duty Cycle Definitions

| Code | Name | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| **S1** | Continuous Duty | Motor works at constant load long enough to reach thermal equilibrium |
| **S2** | Short-Time Duty | Motor works at constant load but not long enough to reach thermal equilibrium; long rest periods allow cooling to ambient temperature |
| **S3** | Intermittent Periodic Duty | Sequential, identical run and rest cycles at constant load; thermal equilibrium never reached |
| **S4** | Intermittent Periodic Duty with Starting | Sequential, identical start, run and rest cycles at constant load; thermal equilibrium not reached; starting current affects temperature rise |
| **S5** | Intermittent Periodic Duty with Electric Braking | Sequential cycles of starting, running at constant load, and running with no load; no rest periods |
| **S6** | Continuous Operation with Intermittent Load | Sequential cycles of running at constant load and running with no load; no rest periods |
| **S7** | Continuous Operation with Electric Braking | Sequential cycles of starting, running at constant load, and electric braking; no rest periods |
| **S8** | Continuous Operation with Periodic Load/Speed Changes | Sequential duty cycles run at different constant loads and speeds; no rest periods |

## Key Considerations

- **S1** is the baseline continuous duty cycle
- **S2-S4** include rest periods for cooling
- **S5-S8** are continuous operation cycles with no rest periods
- Thermal characteristics vary significantly between cycles
- Motor selection must match the actual duty cycle requirements
